text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Editorial says Albania's situation in 1997 is not too different from the crisis which the country faced six years ago when protesters toppled the late communist leader Enver Hoxha's statue in Tirana.

- A delegation of students from the southern town of Vlore will meet President Sali Berisha on Thursday in a bid to resolve the crisis in their town after talks with parliament speaker Pjeter Arbnori failed on Wednesday.
- Some 60 Vlore students threatened to start a hunger strike if the government does not fulfil demands to resolve the crisis created by the failure of pyramid schemes.

- A meeting between the ruling Democratic Party and the opposition Socialists was cancelled after the opposition said it wanted a number of demands, such as the resignation of the government, to be met first.
- President Berisha, unlikely to face a rival candidate, is set to be re-elected by parliament no later than March 9, one month before his current term expires, the paper says in a commentary.
- The Albanian government has not asked for international financial assistance to overcome the crisis created by the failure of pyramid schemes.
- Anti-government protests continued in the southern towns of Tepelene and Gramsh, while teachers in the north went on strike.
- The family of Artur Rustemi, shot dead last week during riots in Vlore, blame the government for his death.
- Vefa Holding, the country's biggest company, says it would start to return capital to investors.

- The opposition Forum for Democracy alliance will hold a rally at a Tirana soccer stadium on Thursday. It has asked authorities for permission for another meeting on Saturday and said it would invite President Berisha for roundtable talks.
- In a meeting in the central town of Elbasan, Berisha reiterated that new elections would not be held before the year 2000.
- Protestors in the southern town of Fier decided not to stage a demonstration on Wednesday for fear of a crackdown by security forces.
